description:
## Sites

apps/octo_pi_tui/lib/octo_pi/tui/interactive.ex
\`\`\`elixir
defp message_text(%{content: c}) when is_binary(c), do: c
defp message_text(%{content: c}) when is_list(c) do
  Enum.map_join(c, \"\\n\", fn ... end)
end
defp message_text(other), do: inspect(other)
\`\`\`
The first clause was added in opi-tze.3 specifically because of the
dual-shape ambiguity. After opi-5ka.3 the binary clause is dead code.
Collapse to the list-shape clause; the catch-all stays for
defensive programming against malformed inputs from extensions.

apps/octo_pi_coder/lib/octo_pi/coder/components/tree_selector.ex
\`\`\`elixir
defp extract_content_text(s) when is_binary(s), do: normalize_text(s)
defp has_text_content?(s) when is_binary(s), do: String.trim(s) != \"\"
\`\`\`
Same treatment.

apps/octo_pi_coder/lib/octo_pi/coder/session/message_writer.ex
\`\`\`elixir
defp user_content(text) when is_binary(text), do: [%{\"type\" => \"text\", \"text\" => text}]
\`\`\`
This one is on the writer side: it converts an in-memory message
into the JSON shape persisted to disk. Since post-5ka.3 in-memory
content is always list-shape, the binary clause is dead. Drop it.
(NB: the on-disk JSON writer can still emit the string shorthand
for User entries if upstream interop demands it — that's a JSON-
emission concern, separate from Elixir struct content shape.)

## Tests
- Updated in opi-5ka.3 already.
- Verify tmux probe still works (queue indicator + restore-to-editor
  + escape-restore all still render correctly).

## Depends on
opi-5ka.3.
title: Drop dual-shape branches in TUI / tree_selector / message_writer
